Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as fd6e299a116851e0b47d7dfc0889942b3419b7bc
Please add this to phosphor-dbus-interfaces instead of getting properties and types by hand.

I have submitted the interface definition to phosphor-dbus-interfaces: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/89727

The implementation in this patch has been updated to use the auto-generated sdbusplus::async client proxy. This replaces the manual D-Bus property fetching and variant parsing, ensuring type safety and adhering to the recommended sdbusplus::async patterns.
Please fix the mode on all of the files you just added.  There is no reason for them to be marked executable.
The file permissions have already been corrected.
Why are we doing this?  lg2 has a debug output.

Originally, this was added to provide more detailed debug output during development, and it could later be controlled via a #define DEBUG switch. Since the development is now complete, I have removed this part.
Why aren't you using the generated bindings to get these properties?
I have updated the implementation to use the generated bindings to access the properties as suggested. Please let me know if further changes are needed.
Please add the related PRs from EntityManager (Schema, Configuration) and phosphor-dbus-interfaces (device compatible strings) related to this addition as Related PRs section.
I have added the related Entity-Manager PR to the Related PRs section in the commit message.
Please verify and add a section stating the CPLD version update is sticking after an AC cycle
I have tested and verified that the updated CPLD version successfully persists and sticks across a full AC power cycle, and documented this in the commit message Tested section.
Done
Since all these are static and private, better to move these to cpp file?
Done. I've moved all static constexpr variables from max10_cpld.hpp into an anonymous namespace in max10_cpld.cpp.
why unused? i see you are using this.
Please follow the coding conventions for variable names throughout the patch https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/cpp-style-and-conventions.md#variables
Fixed all variables throughout the patch to adhere to OpenBMC variable naming guidelines (lowerCamelCase).

Since our design now fully relies on the upper-layer framework's MuxOutputs to automatically toggle GPIO/Mux, we no longer perform any manual D-Bus GPIO lookup inside Max10CPLD.

I have completely removed the ctx_ member variable from the class. For the unused ctx parameter in the constructor, I have commented out the parameter name in max10_cpld.cpp which is the standard C++ way to suppress compilation warnings.

Please create a related PR section and add links to PRs for -
- EM schema changes
- EM Configuration changes
- phosphor-dbus-interfaces changes for compatible strings
Please ignore this, i found the related PRs in Topic search.
it can just be max10Type, isn't it?

Thank you for the suggestion. I have applied this naming convention throughout the codebase, including the helper functions (e.g., renamed getMax10ChipStr to getMax10ChipName) and internal variables to remove redundant 'Str'/'String' suffixes and improve clarity.

Whats this for? As written its hard to understand whats the purpose of this. Looks like u r trying to say that some data can represent either a model or a type, if yes, then it makes sense to avoid the word String from there, isn't it?
Done. I agree that 'String' is redundant here. I have renamed max10StringType to max10Type and updated the enum members accordingly to keep it clean and descriptive.
I don't see any change in existing files which is hooking up altera to existing flow, why is that ?
Please ignore this, i figured it out.
How will caller handle empty string ? Do they check for it being empty?
Good catch. Added an empty string check if (typeName.empty()) { continue; } inside the factory registration loop to properly handle and skip unsupported chip types.
Is this some data or register type if yes, then lets name it max10DataType or something like that to better reflect the intent.
Done. Renamed max10Type to max10DataType to better reflect that it indicates the type of data (Model or Type) to retrieve.
Any reason u r not defining this as a base class ?

Currently, there is no shared state or inherited behavior required across different MAX10 models, so standalone helper functions and enums are sufficient and simpler. The file acts as a shared definitions header between the Factory and the CPLD
Why unused ?
Removed the unused statusBusyRead and statusReadSuccess variables to clean up the code.
Why not calling this openDevice to bring it in sync with closeDevice?
Done. Renamed ensureOpen to openDevice to keep it in sync with closeDevice.
no sync sleep, please change to async sleep, refer to lattice CPLD code for reference.

Done. Converted all hardware I/O and polling functions (readReg, writeReg, eraseSector, etc.) to return sdbusplus::async::task<bool>. Restored the ctx context member in Max10CPLD and replaced all synchronous std::this_thread::sleep_for calls with co_await sdbusplus::async::sleep_for.

Probably u can use lg2::hex https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/phosphor-power/phosphor-power-supply/power_supply.cpp?r=c17ae2d037d3dbe465f47fcf7eb0d40a119a4f93#247

and avoid defining a local var.
Done. Removed the local regStr buffer and the toHex8 helper. Utilized lg2::hex directly in the logging statements.
Please define a constexpr for 100, do same for all other constant values u have used in the file.
no sync sleep, please change to async sleep, refer to lattice CPLD code for reference.
Done. Defined constexpr variables at the top of the file for all retry limits and sleep durations.
Done.
no sync sleep, please change to async sleep, refer to lattice CPLD code for reference.
Done.

Probably u can use lg2::hex https://grok.openbmc.org/xref/openbmc/phosphor-power/phosphor-power-supply/power_supply.cpp?r=c17ae2d037d3dbe465f47fcf7eb0d40a119a4f93#247

and avoid defining a local var.
Done.
no sync sleep, please change to async sleep, refer to lattice CPLD code for reference.
Done.
no sync sleep, please change to async sleep, refer to lattice CPLD code for reference.
Done.
no sync sleep, please change to async sleep, refer to lattice CPLD code for reference.
Done.
Whats the purpose of this comment ?
Done. Removed the redundant comment as the endianness byte-swapping logic is self-explanatory.
Please don't include Meta specific comments here. This should follow standard altera spec.
Done. Removed the Meta-specific comments and generalized the description to standard Avalon-MM IP Offsets.
Please define constexpr for 0x04 and use it at other places too.
Done. Defined constexpr uint32_t ctrlRegOffset = 0x04; to represent the Control Register offset as per the Altera specification and replaced all instances of 0x04 with this constant.

Please define constexpr for 0x7U and 20 defining its purpose.

Please do same for any other such unnamed constants in the patch.
Done. Defined constexpr uint32_t sectorEraseMask = 0x7U; and constexpr uint32_t sectorEraseShift = 20; to clearly reflect their purpose in bitwise operations.
Use above defined constexpr for 0x04 here as well.
Done.
What is 4? Please define a constexpr for it.
Done. The 4 represents the 4-byte word size used for writing data through the Avalon-MM bridge. I've defined constexpr uint32_t wordSize = 4; and replaced the magic numbers in the loop accordingly.
Whats 3 ? Please define a constexpr for it.

Done. The 3 is used for boundary checking to ensure there are enough bytes left in the buffer to form a full 4-byte word before packing. I've replaced it with wordSize - 1 to make the logic self-explanatory.
Would it make sense to rename both .hpp and .ccp to max10_standard_cpld to use similar naming convention as lattice for standard versions?
Good point. Renamed the class to Max10StandardCPLD and the files to max10_standard_cpld.hpp/.cpp. Aligning with the Lattice CPLD naming convention avoids confusion and makes the architecture clearer.

Whats the source of the environment variables that you are trying to read here?

Why do you need this ?

Reading hardware offsets from environment variables is not a standard practice for OpenBMC daemons. Since the default profile already covers our target hardware, I have completely removed the parseEnvUnsigned and loadProfileFromEnv logic to keep it simple and clean.
Why do u want to erase if u r going to error out on unprotectSector failure, can you please handle this flow better. As written this 0/1 logic is hard to read and understand.

Done. You are right; attempting an erase after an unprotect failure is pointless. I have removed the cryptic 0/1 bitwise logic and replaced it with standard boolean checks (if (!(...))) to improve readability and ensure the operations are evaluated logically.
You are checking if ret != 0, which means if either of the above 2 operations fail, i think u should do a better handling in code path above.

Done. I have refactored the error handling to short-circuit immediately. By using if (!(co_await unprotectSector(...)) || !(co_await eraseSector(...))), the function now logs the specific error and returns false right away upon the first failure, rather than accumulating the error state and checking it at the end of the block.

The way this API is written its really confusing. I had to read it multiple times to understand what its trying to do.

Please break this API into 2 APIs based on its usage. That way u won't even need the max10DataType enum at all.

Done. I agree that using a flag argument makes the API confusing. I have removed the max10DataType enum entirely and split the logic into two explicit APIs: getMax10ModuleName() and getMax10TypeName()
What is 10 and 85 here? Please define constexpr for them.

Done. Defined constexpr int progressBasePct = 10;, constexpr int progressProgramPct = 85;, and constexpr size_t progressUpdateInterval = 1024; to eliminate these magic numbers and clarify the progress calculation logic.
Dont u need an enum for this as u have switch cases ?
Done. Defined an enum class Max10ImageType : uint8_t { cfmImage1 = 1, cfmImage2 = 2, cfmImage3 = 3 }; to ensure type safety and make the switch-case statements more readable.
Please define a single chipNameMap and use it in both the APIs.
Done. Extracted chipNameMap into an anonymous namespace so it is defined only once and shared by both APIs.
Is the EM config name if yes, then lets rename this to getMax10ConfigName

It actually corresponds to the Type field in the Entity-Manager configuration (e.g., "Type": "AlteraMAX10_10M16Firmware"), not the Name field. To make the intent perfectly clear, I have renamed the API to getMax10ConfigType().
nit: lets call this baseProgressPercent and rename other related vars accordingly

Done. Renamed progressBasePct to baseProgressPercent, progressProgramPct to programProgressPercent, progressCompletePct to completeProgressPercent, and progressUpdateInterval to updateProgressInterval to make the naming consistent and descriptive.

nit: rename to completeProgressPercent.

Better move these constexpr locally to that function (if they are used only in a single function). Same for others.

Done. Moved the progress-related constexpr variables locally into the programRpd() function since they are only used there. I also renamed them to baseProgressPercent, programProgressPercent, and completeProgressPercent as suggested. Furthermore, I applied the same logic to move versionReg and versionBufSize locally into getVersion().
nit: rename to progressPercent
Done. Renamed the local variable pct to progressPercent for better clarity.
Why this one has to be an API? You can always define chipNameMap as static constexpe and then use it in the 2 APIs below.Both the callers are just reading it.

You are right. I originally used a function wrapper to avoid the Static Initialization Order Fiasco. However, defining it as a constexpr std::array guarantees compile-time constant initialization, which cleanly avoids the SIOF issue without needing an API. I have updated the map to a constexpr std::array and removed the function.

Why can't the openDevice() be performed/called once in the constructor as u r doing the close in the destructor? I see both of them are private functions.

Right now u r calling openDevice() in every API call ?

Done. Since the Max10StandardCPLD instance is created per operation and short-lived, moving the device opening to the constructor perfectly follows the RAII pattern.
